Most [presidents of the United States](Presidents_of_the_United_States "Presidents of the United States") received a [college education](College_education "College education"), even most of the earliest. Of the first seven presidents, five were college graduates. College degrees have set the presidents apart from the general population, and presidents have held degrees even though it was quite rare and unnecessary for practicing most occupations, including [law](Law "Law"). Of the 45 individuals to have been the president, 25 of them graduated from a private undergraduate college, nine graduated from a public undergraduate college, and 12 held no degree. Every president since 1953 has had a [bachelor's degree](Bachelor's_degree "Bachelor's degree"), reflecting the increasing importance of [higher education in the United States](Higher_education_in_the_United_States "Higher education in the United States").

Bush scored a 1206 out of 1600 on the <SAT>; 566 on the verbal section, and 640 on the math section.[[6]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-6) Bush cheered for both Philips Academy's and Yale's football teams, as it was quite common for cheerleaders to be male in Bush's time.[[7]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-7)[[8]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-8) At Yale, he joined [Delta Kappa Epsilon](Delta_Kappa_Epsilon "Delta Kappa Epsilon"), of which he was from October 1965 until graduation, and the [Skull and Bones](Skull_and_Bones "Skull and Bones") [secret society](Secret_society "Secret society"); Bush's father [George H. W. Bush](George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") (1948) and grandfather [Prescott S. Bush](Prescott_S._Bush "Prescott S. Bush") (1917) were also members of Skull and Bones. Bush was also in the Yale First XV [rugby union](Rugby_union "Rugby union") team in 1968.[[9]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-Rugby_yale-9) He was a C student, scoring 77% (with no As and one D, in astronomy) with a [grade point average](Grade_point_average "Grade point average") of 2.35 out of a possible 4.00. Bush joked that he was known more for his social life than for his grades.[[10]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-10) He received a [Bachelor of Arts](Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") degree in history in 1968. The entire entry from his yearbook read:
> GEORGE BUSH. Born July 6, 1946, in New Haven, Connecticut, son of George H.W. Bush (Class of '48) and Barbara Pierce Bush. Prepared at Phillips Academy-Andover, Andover, Massachusetts. Entered Yale, September, 1964. History Major. Resident Member: Davenport (Social Council, 1964-68; Football, 1964-68, Captain, 1967-68; Baseball, 1965-68); Delta Kappa Epsilon, President, 1966-67; Skull and Bones; Inter- Council, 1966-67; Freshman Baseball, 1965; Rugby Club, 1966-68. Roommates: R.J. Dieter, C. Johnson, III, C. Johnson, Jr. Address: Apt. 8, 5000 Longmont Drive, Houston, Texas 77027.

Bush's 1970 application to the [University of Texas School of Law](University_of_Texas_School_of_Law "University of Texas School of Law") was rejected,[[11]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-11) and after his service in the Texas [Air National Guard](Air_National_Guard "Air National Guard") he entered [Harvard Business School](Harvard_Business_School "Harvard Business School") in 1973. He graduated with a [Master of Business Administration](Master_of_Business_Administration "Master of Business Administration") (MBA) degree in 1975, the first U.S. president with an MBA.

### Rugby

Bush was a keen [rugby union](Rugby_union "Rugby union") player, during high school and [Yale University](Yale_University "Yale University").[[12]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-CainGrowden-12)[[13]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-Ruggers-13) He played at the position of [fullback](Fullback_(rugby_union) "Fullback (rugby union)")[[13]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-Ruggers-13) for Yale's 1st XV, and in 1968 was in the Yale team that dramatically defeated <Harvard>.[[12]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-CainGrowden-12)[[13]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-Ruggers-13)

## Service in the Air National Guard

See also: [George W. Bush military service controversy](George_W._Bush_military_service_controversy "George W. Bush military service controversy")

After graduating from Yale University, Bush joined the Texas [Air National Guard](Air_National_Guard "Air National Guard") on May 27, 1968, during the [Vietnam War](Vietnam_War "Vietnam War"), with a commitment to serve until May 26, 1974. He was promoted to [first lieutenant](First_lieutenant "First lieutenant") on the November 1970 recommendation of Texas Air National Guard commander Lt. Col. [Jerry B. Killian](Jerry_B._Killian "Jerry B. Killian"). He served as an <F-102> pilot until 1972. Bush was discharged from the Texas Air National Guard and transferred to [inactive duty](Individual_Ready_Reserve "Individual Ready Reserve") in the [Air Force Reserve](Air_Force_Reserve_Command "Air Force Reserve Command"). He was [honorably discharged](Honorable_discharge "Honorable discharge") from the Air Force Reserve on November 21, 1974, at the end of his six-year service obligation.[[14]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-14)

## Alcohol use and DUI arrest

Bush had described his days before his [religious conversion](Religious_conversion "Religious conversion") in his 40s as his nomadic period and irresponsible youth. Although Bush states that he was not an [alcoholic](Alcoholic "Alcoholic"), he has acknowledged that he was "drinking too much".[[15]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-kristof-15)

On September 4, 1976, Bush was arrested for [driving under the influence](Driving_under_the_influence "Driving under the influence") of alcohol near his family's summer home in [Kennebunkport, Maine](Kennebunkport%2C_Maine "Kennebunkport, Maine"). He admitted his guilt, was fined [US$](United_States_dollar "United States dollar")150, and had his driving license in the state briefly suspended.[[16]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-16)

During the [2000 presidential campaign](U.S._presidential_election%2C_2000 "U.S. presidential election, 2000"), Bush said that he gave up drinking after waking up with a [hangover](Hangover "Hangover") after his 40th birthday celebration: "I quit drinking in 1986 and haven't had a drop since then." He ascribed the change in part to a 1985 meeting with Reverend [Billy Graham](Billy_Graham "Billy Graham"), after which he began serious <Bible> [study](Bible_study_(Christian) "Bible study (Christian)"), as well as to gentle but persistent pressure from his wife, [Laura](Laura_Bush "Laura Bush").[[17]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-17)[[18]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-18)[[19]](Early_life_of_George_W._Bush#cite_note-19)

## Family life

Main article: [Bush family](Bush_family "Bush family")

Bush married [Laura Welch](Laura_Bush "Laura Bush") in 1977. They have fraternal twin daughters, [Barbara Pierce Bush](Barbara_Bush_(born_1981) "Barbara Bush (born 1981)") and [Jenna Welch Bush Hager](Jenna_Hager "Jenna Hager"), born in 1981.
